# Corporate Law: Crime Listing Crime codes are colored by linked crime groups, which are collections of non-stackable crimes. Non-stackable crimes cannot be charged simultaneously, and a sentence should use the most severe applicable crime in the category.
In the case of violent crimes (06 and 07), only the most severe crime committed against each victim should be charged. In the case of a criminal committing acts of physical violence against multiple victims, each attack can be charged accordingly if they do not involve linked crimes.

## Linked Crimes: Crimes that are linked can not be charged together. For more information, refer to Sentencing.
0. [color=#8b376d]Criminal Procedure[/color]. Covers Failure to Comply, Violation of Parole, Breach of Arrest, Breach of Custody, Refusal of Mental Shielding
1. [color=#458159]Unlawful Possession[/color]. Covers Possession or Use of Minor Contraband, Major Contraband, Highly Illegal Contraband, or Humanoid Tissues/Organs
2. [color=#327e32]Larceny[/color]. Covers Petty Theft, Grand Theft, Armed Robbery, or Theft of Vital Infrastructure
3. [color=#61429a]Property Crime[/color]. Covers Vandalism, Property Damage or Tampering, Destruction of Property, Mass Destruction, or Terrorism
4. [color=#877f38]Unlawful Entry[/color]. Covers Trespass, Tailgating, or Secure Trespass
5. [color=#6a7896]Rebellion[/color]. Covers Disturbance, Vigilantism, Agitation, Rioting, or Revolutionary Activity
6. [color=#ac3a54]Violence[/color]. Covers Assault/Cruelty, Battery, Aggravated Assault, Attempted Murder, or Unlawful Execution/Prevention of Revival
7. [color=#8e3535]Risk to Life[/color]. Covers Criminal Negligence, Reckless Endangerment, Manslaughter, Murder, or Mass Murder
8. [color=#c9c9c9]Fraudulence[/color]. Covers Fraud, Bribery, Forgery/Perjury, Unlawful Imprisonment, or Mind Control
9. [color=#df8348]Impersonation[/color]. Covers Impersonation, of Security, of Command, or of Corporate
10. [color=#4472ba]Corporate Crime[/color]. Covers Insubordination/Malfeasance, Conspiracy, Sedition, Treason, or Enemy of Corporation
## Minor Crimes Those who commit a minor crime should be issued a warning for their first offense, however repeat offenses are cumulative and should result in jail time of up to 5 minutes per minor crime committed.
Offense
Description
Failure to Comply
To resist reasonable orders given by an authority. This includes lawful detainment and authorized searches. Officers are required to warn the individual before resorting to arrest.
Possession or Use of Minor Contraband
To make, hold, or use minor contraband without authorization. Department or Job restricted decorative items (e.g. uniforms, belts and bags, and boxcutters) are considered minor contraband.
Petty Theft
To take non-vital or inexpensive property of another individual, organization, or common property, without consent. Theft of safety or medical equipment such as breath masks, air tanks, or necessary mobility aids are considered vital, and exceed petty theft.
Vandalism
To intentionally deface or superficially damage public or private property. Examples include graffiti, smashing glasses or windows, excessively littering, and excessively producing spills. Art or construction with an appropriate permit is not vandalism.
Trespass
To enter a non-secured area without permission, such as climbing over counters to enter employee areas like the Bar or Kitchen or entering locked non-secure areas using a crowbar during blackouts.
Disturbance
To cause a public disturbance. This is the catch-all for excessive obnoxious behavior, and includes public nudity, harassment, inciting crime, repeated and intentional misgendering, and disruption of authorities or communications.
Assault/Cruelty
To assault another without a weapon, or to inflict unnecessary suffering or harm on a non-humanoid being with malicious intent. This does not include legitimate and authorized animal testing, butchering of livestock for meat, or elimination of vermin and hostile creatures.
Criminal Negligence
To cause loss to an individual through incompetence, unreasonable inaction, or subpar work. This should be charged for ineptitude or workplace accidents, and not for malicious activity or endangerment.
Fraud
To attempt to commit fraud in any fashion. Fraudulent activities include but are not limited to selling departmental equipment for personal profit, and engaging in scamming.
Impersonation
To pretend to be someone you are not. Extra penalties should be added for committing an act of impersonation using illegal equipment such as vocal modifiers or stolen identification.
Insubordination or Malfeasance
To willingly disobey a lawful order from a superior (as dictated by Departmental and Job SOP), or engage in misconduct or wrongful activity as a member of Security or Command.
## Moderate Crimes Those who commit a moderate crime should receive up to a 5 minute sentence per moderate crime committed.
Offense
Description
Violation of Parole
To fail to comply with a lawful, clearly communicated order to report to Security while under parole. This can only be charged five or more minutes after the order was given.
Possession or Use of Major Contraband
To make, hold, or use major contraband without authorization. Any Department or Job restricted functional items (e.g. RCDs, firearms, fultons) are considered major contraband.
Grand Theft
To take critical or irreplaceable property of another individual or organization without consent. This includes command items such as door remotes, hardsuits, machine parts, and hijacking a department shuttle.
Property Damage or Tampering
To damage the integrity or functionality of equipment or structures through deconstruction, wire-snipping, or physical force. Includes but is not limited to consoles, airlocks, walls, and Silicons. Certain wire tampering is permissible based on severity, role of the offender, and offending context.
Tailgating
To follow an individual into a department without sufficient access or permission. This applies to following coworkers through locked airlocks. If the area entered is considered Secure, charge with Secure Trespass instead.
Vigilantism
To attempt to enforce Corporate Law without vested authority. This charge applies to any non-deputised, non-Security personnel who attempt to make an arrest, to enact frontier justice, or to otherwise take Corporate Law into their own hands without authorisation.
Battery
To assault another without use of a deadly weapon, resulting in serious injury to the victim. Serious injury is defined as any life altering injury such as loss of limb, damage to the eyes or ears, or any other damages measured by a Health Analyzer to be exceeding 30 total.
Reckless Endangerment
To recklessly put oneself or others in danger, either through direct action or failure to act. This includes negligence, accidents, medical malpractice, destruction or impairment of safety features such as firelocks and exterior windows, and reckless piloting of shuttles.
Bribery
To attempt or succeed to bribe officials to be derelict of their duties or commit a crime with any payment including but not limited to; Services, favors, spesos, credits, materials, or items of any kind. This also applies to anyone caught accepting a bribe, and is cumulative with whatever crime they were bribed to commit.
Impersonation: Security
To pretend to be a member of the Security Department. Extra penalties should be added for committing an act of impersonation using illegal equipment such as vocal modifiers or stolen identification.
Conspiracy
To willingly aid in or plan to commit a major crime with other individuals. If multiple individuals are implicated in a criminal conspiracy, they should also be charged appropriately.
## Major Crimes Those who commit a major crime should receive up to 10 minutes of jail time per major crime committed. Aggravated Assault and Manslaughter do not stack against a suspect.
Offense
Description
Breach of Arrest
To intentionally resist and flee arrest or detainment by an authorized staff. This only applies if someone is actively being physically arrested. This charge also applies to uncuffing an arrested individual or assisting others out of an arrest.
Possession or Use of Highly Illegal Contraband
To make, hold, or use highly illegal contraband without authorization. Any equipment manufactured by non-NT certified providers typically falls under this category.
Armed Robbery
To steal something with the threat of violence using anything that can be considered a weapon, regardless of the item's contraband status. There must be an active threat of violence or the implication of violence if the victim does not comply in order to be considered armed robbery.
Destruction of Property
To destroy the property of another or the station. This includes but is not limited to work consoles, airlocks, and destroying or critically damaging a Cyborg's chassis.
Secure Trespass
To enter a secured area without permission. This includes but is not limited to the Engineering department for non-Engineers, Telecomms, AI Core, Department Head offices, Bridge, Vault, and Security department for non-Security personnel.
Rioting
To participate in a large group of personnel creating an unlawful public disturbance. This can involve conventional riots, strikes and similar industrial action, and organised and coordinated resistance against the station authority.
Aggravated Assault
To assault another with a deadly weapon, or to commit assault resulting in life-threatening injury. life-threatening injury is defined as any damages measured by a Health Analyzer to be exceeding 60 total.
Manslaughter
To incidentally kill a sentient humanoid without intent. This includes manslaughter in self-defense and negligent manslaughter.
Forgery and Perjury
To forge a written document through illicit means, intentionally lie under oath or make a false statement in a written document. This includes but is not limited to rewriting a stamped document or misusing an official stamp.
Impersonation: Command
To pretend to be a member of Station Command. Extra penalties should be added for committing an act of impersonation using illegal equipment such as vocal modifiers or stolen identification.
Sedition
To incite rebellion or disseminate propaganda encouraging rebellion against the authority of the station. If seditious action led to the outbreak of mass disturbance or rioting, Agitation should be charged instead.
## Extreme Crimes Those who commit an extreme crime may receive up to 20 minutes of jail time per extreme crime committed. Particularly violent offenders may be placed in permanent confinement. Attempted Murder and Murder cannot be stacked together.
Offense
Description
Breach of Custody
To break out of a cell or custody with the intention of escaping, or to assist in a breakout. Repeat offenses may have this charge increased to permanent confinement. Breach of custody for the preservation of life (not including to escape execution) may be reduced or ignored at the Warden or Head of Security's discretion.
Possession or of Humanoid Tissues or Organs
To unlawfully possess or consume any part of a sentient humanoid. Possession or consumption of vital components should be treated more harshly. This can be charged on top of other charges such as Murder or Assault if the suspect committed these crimes to obtain the parts. Any act of cannibalism falls under this category.
Theft of Vital Infrastructure
To steal a vital and irreplaceable structure or item necessary for the station's operation, such as the Research Server, Crew Monitoring Server, Nuclear Fission Explosive, Nuclear Authentication Disk, Station AI, or Thermo-Electric Generator.
Mass Destruction
To cause massive damage to an area or major station system. This includes major bombings and sabotage of critical station systems like power, medical, chemistry, substations, and atmospherics.
Agitation
To cause the outbreak of a rebellion, strike, or other large-scale riot, either through direct leadership, incessant incitement, or subversive methods. An Agitation charge also permits charging for all crimes committed under the criminal's lead.
Attempted Murder
To make an attempt to end someone's life, using physical force or otherwise. Proof that action was taken with the intent to kill is necessary, such as a lethal weapon being used.
Murder
To kill a sentient humanoid with malicious intent. If the victim must be revived, it is murder and not attempted murder.
Unlawful Imprisonment
To unlawfully restrain, transport, control, or confine a sentient humanoid being against that individual's will. This extends to any and all forms of kidnapping and unlawful detainment.
Impersonation: Corporate
To pretend to be a member of Central Command, NanoTrasen, or any other Government or Corporate official. Extra penalties should be added for committing an act of impersonation using illegal equipment such as vocal modifiers or stolen identification.
Treason
To willfully betray allegiances to NanoTrasen. This includes collaborating with terrorists, and especially applies to members of Command attempting to illegally forsake their duties to the detriment of the Station and Nanotrasen.
## Capital Crimes Those who commit a capital crime should be detained in permanent confinement with confirmation from the Captain. If a capital criminal escapes they are to be executed and transported to CC in a body bag at the end of shift. Emergency executions may be enacted by the Captain or the Head of Security with at least 3 other Command as witnesses, but must be reported directly to Central Command afterward for review.
Offense
Description
Refusal of Mental Shielding
To refuse to comply with a reasonable Mind Shielding procedure within the context of Martial Law. Applies only if the suspect is excessively uncooperative or the implant fails to function due to the mental state of the prisoner being too far gone.
Terrorism
To engage in malicious destructive actions which threaten to destroy or successfully destroy a vessel, habitat, or station. This includes extreme sabotage of station systems or setting off the self-destruction systems.
Revolutionary Activity
To act in a leading capacity on behalf of a large-scale revolt against the station authority. This includes enacting industrial-scale sabotage, supplying revolters with arms, and driving a riot forward with extremist rhetoric.
Unlawful Execution
To unlawfully execute an individual without authorization or outside of Standard Operating Procedure. This law is distinct from murder, and applies primarily to Security, Command, and Central Command forces such as Emergency Response Teams.
Prevention of Revival
To render a body un-resurrectable. This includes destroying a body, throwing a body into space, intentionally hiding a body, unlawfully incinerating a body, committing cannibalism, or any other ways of preventing a body with a soul from being resurrected.
Mass Murder
To kill three or more sentient humanoids with malicious intent. Only applies when there have been multiple killings with intention.
Mind Control
To use any form of mind controlling technique or technology to force an individual to act against their will. This only applies beyond a shadow of a doubt.
Enemy of Corporation
To act directly on behalf of a known enemy of the Station and/or of NanoTrasen. This only applies against individuals confirmed as such by Central Command, or individuals engaging in an act of Terrorism on behalf of an enemy organisation.
